plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the agent–environment interaction loop in reinforcement learning, depicted as a closed directed cycle between two rounded rectangular boxes filled with light teal. The upper box is labeled “Agent” with the policy π[a_t | s_t] inscribed inside, and the lower, larger box is labeled “Environment” with the state transition probability Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) inscribed inside. Orange arrows with arrowheads form the loop: one arrow routes from the Agent box rightward and downward into the Environment box, carrying the action a_t; a second arrow returns from the Environment to the Agent carrying the current state s_t, while a third routes the next state s_{t+1} back around; additional arrow paths carry rewards r_t and r_{t+1}, and a label identifies the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t). Small white-background rectangles along the arrow paths isolate variable labels — State, Action, and Reward — for readability. This figure introduces the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework at the core of reinforcement learning, showing how the agent observes a state, selects an action according to its policy, and receives a reward and next state from the environment in a repeating closed loop.

interactionPlan.concept: The Markov Decision Process (MDP) formalizes reinforcement learning as a continuous feedback loop where an agent's actions influence the environment, which in turn provides the next state and reward.

interactions.label: Step through MDP loop
interactions.teaches: The sequential causality of the loop: receiving the state/reward, choosing an action, and the environment computing the next state.
The agent's internal mechanics: it uses a policy to map the currently observed state to a chosen action.
The environment's mechanics: it uses internal transition and reward probabilities to determine what happens next based on the state and action.

demo_steps.title: The MDP Loop
demo_steps.narration: The Markov Decision Process (MDP) models reinforcement learning as a continuous loop between an agent and its environment.

demo_steps.title: Observation
demo_steps.narration: The cycle begins when the agent observes the current state and receives the latest reward from the environment.

demo_steps.title: Action
demo_steps.narration: Using its policy, the agent decides on an action based on the state it observed, and sends this action back to the environment.

demo_steps.title: Environment Transition
demo_steps.narration: The environment processes the action and current state to compute the next state and reward, ready for the next time step.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Reinforcement learning is a closed causal loop: the agent's actions alter the environment, which in turn defines the agent's next observation and reward.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Layout is vertical: Agent box above Environment box. Boxes are light teal with thin black borders. Arrows are a distinct copper/orange color with clear arrowheads indicating flow direction. The flow forms a closed circuit: moving UP on the left from Env to Agent, and DOWN on the right from Agent to Env. Ensure text labels on arrows have white background rectangles so they visibly occlude the lines beneath them for readability. The vertical dashed line on the left is important: it marks the temporal boundary where outputs from step t (t+1) become the inputs for the next step t. Math variables should be in standard italic serif.

discrepancies: The s_{t+1} and r_{t+1} labels are placed directly over the horizontal lines, breaking them with opaque white backgrounds, whereas the source places them cleanly above unbroken lines.

The simulated math text (e.g. π[a_t|s_t]) has uneven kerning and lacks proper spacing around symbols like the pipe (|) or commas.
